name: MertFormer ternary CPU-kernel microbenchmark (Galaxy S25, ARM NEON)

scope_boundary.interpretation: Standalone single-op ternary matmul microbenchmark, hand-written for this evidence. Measures one GEMM-class kernel on real S25 CPU. It does NOT measure full-model tokens/sec, NPU performance, or the canonical bitlinear.py / triton path. It is related performance evidence, not main-architecture performance.

hardware.note: Single-thread; no multi-core. Numbers are from the physical device, NOT emulation.

build.flags: -O3 (SDOT turbo auto-enabled via inline-asm + runtime HWCAP detection; optional -march=armv8.2-a+dotprod)
build.fairness: float baseline and ternary kernels share identical N/ITERS/data/seed; ground truth computed in double precision

tiers.note: Mathematically identical to float baseline (x*w exact for w in {-1,0,1}); diff = 0.000e+00. No approximation.
int8-quantized activations via vdotq_s32 (16 MAC/instr). NOT bit-exact. ~0.4% rms error. This is the low-bit deployment-mode number, not an exact result.

does_not_prove: NPU performance (this is CPU/NEON, not NPU)
that the canonical 3.67B model runs at any particular speed

reproducibility.verification: FMA tiers self-check max|kernel - float_naive| = 0 at runtime; SDOT reports rms vs double ground truth
reproducibility.cross_checked: Logic cross-compiled with both gcc-aarch64 and clang and run under qemu-aarch64 before on-device measurement
